look_here_first: Check the stem before the flower head. Bitter sneezeweed is the B028 species with stems that are ridged but NOT winged. Then confirm the very narrow linear leaves and numerous small yellow heads. Variety-level support: var. amarum usually has yellow disc lobes, while var. badium has dark brown to purplish disc lobes.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate, narrow to oblanceolate, mostly entire, often clasping or sessile.

key_traits.label: Heads
key_traits.text: Numerous small heads; rays short, often 3-lobed at the tip and drooping; disk yellow becoming more convex.

key_traits.label: Phyllaries
key_traits.text: Appressed to slightly spreading, in several series.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Cypselae with small scales and often minute awns.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: stems ridged/striated but not winged by decurrent leaf tissue

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves numerous, alternate and very narrow linear to threadlike; lower early leaves may be dissected

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: rays usually 8–10, yellow and often reflexed/drooping

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: var. amarum: disc flowers/lobes yellow; more eastern/central Texas pattern

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: var. badium: distal disc lobes brown to purplish; more western/central Texas pattern
